title: Kerala Assembly Walks Out Over 'Dual Justice' Charge After Cheranalloor Hit-and-Run
excerpt: Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan accused Kerala Police of one standard for the rich and another for the poor after a street vendor was killed by a car driven by a minor, the son of a judge, and the Assembly rejected an adjournment motion on police excesses.
body:
• The Kerala Assembly rejected an adjournment motion on alleged police excesses on Tuesday and the Opposition walked out after the Speaker denied permission following the Home Minister's reply.
  • At the centre of the row is the death of Jayabalakrishnan, 55, a street food vendor killed at Cheranalloor around 2:30 a.m. on Sunday by a Mercedes-Benz driven by a minor, the son of a sitting judge.
  • Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan said police initially booked less serious offences and the accused secured bail, asking whether there is one standard of justice for the rich and another for ordinary people.
  • Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said the government took the incident seriously and would not protect anyone responsible, irrespective of position or influence.

The Kerala Legislative Assembly saw heated exchanges on Tuesday after CPI(M) MLA A. C. Moideen moved an adjournment motion seeking a discussion on alleged police excesses and lapses in recent incidents across the state. The Speaker denied permission to take up the motion following Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala's response, prompting the Opposition to stage a walkout, according to ANI via Daily Prabhat.

The Cheranalloor case

Jayabalakrishnan, 55, was killed around 2:30 a.m. on Sunday at Cheranalloor when a Mercedes-Benz car driven by a minor, the son of a judge, struck him. Police initially booked less serious offences and the accused secured bail, triggering allegations of preferential treatment and procedural failure, according to IANS via hi INDiA.

"That child had to ask whether there is one standard of justice for the rich and another for people like them. This happened even before the funeral pyre had cooled."

— Pinarayi Vijayan, Opposition leader, in the Assembly

Vijayan told the Assembly that police had failed to change their conduct despite Chennithala having taken a strong public stance after an earlier accident at Nedumbassery. "The police are not even accepting the words and position taken by the Home Minister," he said, referring to the question raised by Jayabalakrishnan's daughter over whether the rich and ordinary people are treated differently under the law.

A wider charge sheet

The motion was not confined to one crash. Moideen referred to media reports alleging that a ruling-front MLA had intervened in the Nedumbassery case — a remark that triggered protests from the treasury benches and was expunged from the Assembly records by the Speaker. He also cited alleged assaults on students at a university hostel, questioned the circumstances under which a judge had visited a police station in connection with the Cheranalloor case, and said several incidents in recent months pointed to serious shortcomings in policing.

That breadth is what turned a single hit-and-run into a debate about the system: the Opposition's argument is that the initial charges in the FIR, the speed of bail and the alleged interventions form a pattern, not an isolated error.

The government's reply

Responding to the allegations, Chennithala said the government had taken the Cheranalloor incident seriously and would not protect anyone responsible for wrongdoing, irrespective of their position or influence. The government also maintained that it did not support unequal treatment — a position Vijayan challenged by asking whether it was taking the situation seriously enough in practice.

What happens next will be decided less by Assembly rhetoric than by the case file: whether the charges against the minor accused are revised, what the investigation records about the first hours after the crash, and whether the promised accountability reaches the officers who handled it. For Jayabalakrishnan's family, those are the measures that will answer the daughter's question.
